# pnv

> A Dart CLI that lets you commit your secrets. Values are AES-256-GCM encrypted in plain-text YAML
> that lives in the repo; only the symmetric key lives outside it. At build time pnv decrypts the
> YAML into `.env`, and from `.env` into a Dart class of `String/int/bool.fromEnvironment` constants
> or a `--dart-define` argument string.
>
> This file is for an AI agent operating in a repo that uses pnv, or being asked to set pnv up.
> `README.md` is the human-facing version; this one is longer because it also carries the edge cases
> and the footguns. Everything below was verified by reading `lib/` and by running the CLI against a
> real project, not by paraphrasing the README — where the two disagree, trust this file and fix the
> README.

pnv is a **dev-time tool**, not a runtime library. It exposes no public Dart API — `lib/` holds only
`lib/src/**` and `lib/utils/constants.dart`, with no library entrypoint, so `import 'package:pnv/pnv.dart'`
does not resolve. If you are asked to "use pnv in code", the answer is that you shell out to the
executable, or you consume the Dart file it generated.

---

## The model, in one pass

```
  pnv create flavor  ──►  <storage>/<flavor>.key        the key. NEVER in the repo.
                                    │
  envs/app.local.yaml               │                   committed. secrets are ciphertext.
    api_key: SECRET;<base64>  ◄─────┤ pnv encrypt
                                    │
                                    ▼ pnv generate env
  dist/app.local.env                                    gitignored. plaintext.
    API_KEY="real-value"
                                    │
              ┌─────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐
              ▼ pnv generate dart                         ▼ pnv to-dart-define
  lib/envs/app.dart                              -DAPI_KEY=real-value ...
    static const apiKey =                        (feed to dart/flutter build)
      String.fromEnvironment('API_KEY');
```

A **flavor** is a named key plus the file-suffix convention that selects it. Flavor `local` owns
`<storage>/local.key` and claims every `*.local.yaml` / `*.local.env`. A flavor may declare
**aliases** — extra suffixes that resolve to the same key — so flavor `production` with alias `ci`
means `app.ci.yaml` decrypts with `production.key`.

---

## Install and invoke

```bash
dart pub global activate pnv          # then: pnv <command>
dart pub add pnv --dev                # then: dart run pnv <command>
```

The binary is `bin/pnv.dart`. Note that its own usage text calls itself `secrets`
(`CommandRunner('secrets', ...)` in `lib/src/pnv_runner.dart`) — cosmetic only, the command is `pnv`.

Two global flags are stripped in `main()` before argument parsing, so they work in any position:
`--loud` (verbose) and `--quiet`. No `--version`.

Exit code is `0` on success, `1` on any failure, including a wrong decryption key.

### Non-interactive safety — read this before scripting pnv

`pnv init`, `pnv create flavor` on an **existing** flavor, and `pnv delete flavor` without `--force`
all prompt via `mason_logger`, which throws without a TTY:

```
Bad state: No terminal attached to stdout.
```

**Safe to run head-less:** `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `create key`, `generate env`, `generate dart`,
`to-dart-define`, `create flavor --name <new-name>` (a name not already in `.pnvrc`).

**Never safe head-less:** `init` (always prompts, even with everything already configured), and any
`create flavor` / `delete flavor` that hits a confirmation.

To set a project up in a non-interactive context, write `.pnvrc` yourself (it is plain JSON, format
below) and call `create flavor --name <name>` per flavor. Do not reach for `init`.

---

## `.pnvrc`

JSON despite the name. Located **next to `pubspec.yaml`** — pnv walks up from the cwd to find
`pubspec.yaml` and looks for `.pnvrc` in that directory; only if no `pubspec.yaml` exists anywhere
above does it walk up looking for `.pnvrc` directly. It is created/rewritten by `init`,
`create flavor`, and `delete flavor`.

```json
{
  "storage": "~/.my_project",
  "flavors": {
    "local": [],
    "production": ["prod", "ci"]
  }
}
```

- `storage` — directory holding `<flavor>.key` files. A leading `~` expands to `$HOME`
  (`%USERPROFILE%` on Windows). **Commit `.pnvrc`; never commit the storage directory.**
- `flavors` — map of flavor name → alias suffixes. Flavor names are validated against
  `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` when created.
- **Every flavor name and every alias must be globally unique across the map.** A duplicate makes
  `PnvConfig.fromJson` throw `Flavors have conflicts...` and *every* command that loads the config
  fails with exit 1 — including `encrypt`. If pnv suddenly refuses everything, check for a repeated
  alias first.

---

## Commands

Verified against `lib/src/commands/**` and by running each one.

### Key selection — shared by `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `generate env`

Every one of these accepts `--key/-k`, `--key-file/-f`, `--flavor`. Resolution order, first match
wins (`CrypticCommand.secretFor`):

1. `--key <base64>` — the key literal.
2. `--key-file <path>` — file contents, trimmed.
3. `--flavor <name>` — `<storage>/<name>.key`; if that file is absent, pnv searches `.pnvrc` for the
   flavor whose alias list contains `<name>` and uses *that* flavor's key file.

With none of the three: `Invalid argument(s): Missing key, key file, or flavor.` — except
`generate env --file`, which falls back to inferring the flavor from the filename (see below).

There is effectively **no key validation**. `validateSecretKey` checks that a SHA-256 digest is 32
bytes long, which is always true, so any string Dart's base64 decoder accepts is taken as a key —
`--key aaaa` (3 bytes) encrypts and round-trips happily. A non-base64 key fails with a
`FormatException`, not a helpful message. A *wrong* key fails at decrypt time with
`Failed to decrypt value. Do you have the correct key?`.

### `pnv init`

Interactive only. Prompts for the storage directory (default `~/.<pubspec name>`), adopts any
`*.key` files already in that directory as flavors, offers to create key files for flavors listed in
`.pnvrc` that have none, then loops prompting for more flavors. Writes `.pnvrc`.

### `pnv create key`

Prints a fresh key to stdout and does nothing else — no file, no config. 12 cryptographically random
bytes (`Random.secure`), base64url-encoded → a 16-character string like `kx_iAQ-nMD_72wfJ`.

**That is 96 bits of entropy**, not 256. The AES-256 key is `SHA-256(base64decode(keyfile))`, so the
cipher is AES-256 but the secret behind it is 96-bit. Fine against offline guessing; worth knowing if
someone asks you whether this is "a 256-bit key".

### `pnv create flavor --name <name> [--force]`

Writes `<storage>/<name>.key` with a fresh key and adds the flavor to `.pnvrc`. Prompts (⇒ dies
head-less) if the name is already in `.pnvrc`. With no `--name` it prompts for one.

`--force/-f` is declared in the arg parser and **never read by `run()`** — it does not suppress the
overwrite prompt. Do not rely on it.

### `pnv delete flavor [--name <n>]... [--force]`

Deletes the key file and the `.pnvrc` entry. `--name/-n` is repeatable. Without any `--name` it
presents a multi-select prompt of existing flavors. Without `--force/-f` it asks to confirm each one.
Irreversible: the key is gone, and every secret encrypted with it is unreadable forever.

### `pnv encrypt <value>... [key selection]`

Aliases: `enc`, `e`, `encode`. Encrypts each positional argument and writes one `SECRET;...` line per
value to stdout. Quote your values; a value with no positionals throws
`No values to encrypt provided.`

```bash
pnv encrypt "my api key" --flavor local
pnv encrypt --key-file ~/.myapp/local.key "$(pbpaste)"
```

### `pnv decrypt <value>... [key selection]`

Aliases: `dec`, `d`, `decode`. One plaintext line per argument. The `SECRET;` prefix is optional to
strip — pass the token exactly as it appears in the YAML.

### `pnv generate env` — YAML ⇒ `.env`

```
-i, --file <file.yaml>      one input file (aliases: --input)
-d, --directory <dir>       every file in a directory (aliases: --dir)
-o, --output <dir>          output directory      (default: "outputs")
-k/-f/--flavor              key selection (above)
```

At least one of `--file` / `--directory` is required. Output file name is
`<input basename minus its last extension>.env` — `app.local.yaml` ⇒ `app.local.env`, **not**
`local.env` as the README's examples claim. The output directory is created if missing and is *not*
wiped.

Key selection per mode:

- **`--file` with no key flags** — pnv derives the flavor from the filename and looks it up. So
  `pnv generate env -i envs/app.local.yaml -o dist` just works when flavor `local` exists.
- **`--directory`** — with `--flavor`, only files whose filename-flavor is that flavor or one of its
  aliases are processed, all with that flavor's key. With no `--flavor`, **every** file is processed
  and each one's key is derived from its own filename — this is the "regenerate everything" mode.

Filename ⇒ flavor (`FileMixin.flavorFrom`): if the basename has no dot, it *is* the flavor
(`local.yaml` ⇒ `local`); otherwise the second-to-last extension is used
(`app.local.yaml` ⇒ `local`, `infra.staging.env` ⇒ `staging`).

`pnv generate-env` (hyphenated, top-level) is a hidden deprecated alias that prints a warning and
delegates here.

### `pnv generate dart` — `.env` ⇒ Dart class

```
-o, --output <dir>          REQUIRED
-i, --file <file.env>       one input (aliases: --input)
-d, --directory <dir>       input directory (aliases: --dir)
    --flavor <name>         filter --directory by flavor
-c, --class-name <Name>     override the class name; --file only
```

> **The output directory is deleted recursively before writing.** Point it at a directory that
> contains nothing but generated files. pnv aborts with exit 1 only if the directory contains a
> subdirectory; loose unrelated *files* in it are destroyed without warning.

Output file is `<input basename minus extension>.dart` with the flavor segment stripped:
`app.local.env` ⇒ `app.dart`, class `App`. `--class-name` applies only with `--file`.

Precedence inside `run()` is `--file` → `--flavor` (requires `--directory`) → `--directory`, first
match wins and returns.

> **`--directory` without `--flavor` generates only the FIRST file in the directory** — the loop
> returns on its first iteration (`generate_dart_command.dart`). Two `.env` files in, one `.dart`
> out, exit code 0, no warning. Always pass `--flavor` when using `--directory`, or call `--file`
> once per input.

### `pnv to-dart-define <file.env>...`

Reads every file, concatenates the lines, prints a single space-separated
`-DKEY=VALUE -DKEY=VALUE ` string on stdout for `dart`/`flutter build --dart-define`.

> **It silently drops any line whose value contains `=`.** It splits on *every* `=` and skips the
> line unless there are exactly two parts — so `B64="aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ="` never reaches the output.
> Base64 and URL-ish values are the common casualties. Empty values are dropped too. And it does not
> strip trailing type comments, so a `PORT=8080 # int` line becomes `-DPORT=8080 # int`, which the
> build tool will mis-parse. `generate dart` handles all of these correctly (it splits on the first
> `=` only); `to-dart-define` has not been fixed. Prefer `generate dart` where you can.

`pnv create-key` (hyphenated) is a hidden deprecated alias for `create key`.

---

## Formats

### The `SECRET;` token

```
SECRET; + base64( tag[16] || iv[12] || ciphertext[n] || tag[16] )
```

AES-256-GCM. The IV is 12 fresh random bytes per call, so encrypting the same plaintext twice gives
different tokens — expected, not a bug, and it means a re-encrypted YAML always shows a diff. The
128-bit GCM tag appears **twice**: `encrypt_command.dart` prepends `cipher.mac` and PointyCastle's
`process()` has already appended the same tag to the ciphertext. Decryption slices from byte 28 and
ignores the leading copy. Redundant, but stable — do not "fix" it without breaking every existing
secret. There is no version byte and no key id: a token carries nothing that says which flavor
encrypted it.

Key derivation: `AES key = SHA-256(base64decode(<keyfile contents>))`. Constants in
`lib/utils/constants.dart`.

### YAML ⇒ `.env` mapping

```yaml
base-url: http://localhost:3000
app-secret: SECRET;VDlYm6Y2f0wo...
port: 8080
debug: true
db:
  host: localhost
  nested:
    deep-key: deep-value
```

```dotenv
BASE_URL="http://localhost:3000"
APP_SECRET="s3cr3t-value"
PORT=8080
DEBUG=true
# .
# .db
DB_HOST="localhost"
# .
# .db.nested
DB_NESTED_DEEP_KEY="deep-value"
```

- Nested keys are flattened with `_`, uppercased, and `-` becomes `_`.
- **String values are emitted with surrounding double quotes**; `int`, `double`, `bool` are not; a
  null value emits `KEY=` with nothing after it. Any other YAML type (a list, for instance) throws
  `Unsupported value type`. **Lists are not supported.**
- Only string values starting with `SECRET;` are decrypted. Everything else is copied verbatim, so
  non-secret config lives in the same file.
- The `# .` / `# .db` breadcrumb lines are emitted before each nested block. They are comments; the
  `.env` consumers here ignore them.

### Forcing a type (`# int`, `# bool`, `# num`, `# string`)

A trailing YAML comment on a value is carried into the `.env` line and is read back by
`generate dart` as a type declaration. This is how you type a key that is empty in some environments:

```yaml
db:
  port: # int          ⇒  DB_PORT= # int  ⇒  static const dbPort = int.fromEnvironment('DB_PORT');
```

Recognised (case-insensitive): `int` and `num` ⇒ `int.fromEnvironment`, `bool` ⇒
`bool.fromEnvironment`, `string` ⇒ `String.fromEnvironment`. Anything else warns and falls through
to inference. Inference without a declaration: `int.tryParse` succeeds ⇒ int; exactly `true`/`false`
⇒ bool; **everything else ⇒ String, including decimals** — `1.5` becomes
`String.fromEnvironment`, because Dart has no `double.fromEnvironment`.

> **Comment attribution is substring-based and the last match wins.** `envEntriesFromYaml` finds a
> key's comment by scanning the enclosing YAML block for a line *containing* `<key>:`, so a nested
> `db.port: # int` will attach `# int` to an unrelated top-level `port:` further up the same file.
> Symptom: a stray ` # int` in the `.env` and a wrong type in the generated Dart. If you see one,
> rename one of the colliding keys.

### Generated Dart

```dart
// dart format off
// ignore_for_file: lines_longer_than_80_chars

class App {
  const App._();

  static const baseUrl = String.fromEnvironment('BASE_URL');
  static const dbPort = int.fromEnvironment('DB_PORT');
}
```

Keys become `camelCase` fields. These are `fromEnvironment` constants, so **the values are baked in
at compile time from `--dart-define`** — the generated file holds no secrets and is safe to commit.
The `.env` files are the plaintext, and those are what must be gitignored.

---

## Recipes

**Set up a project without prompts.** Write `.pnvrc` next to `pubspec.yaml`, then:

```bash
pnv create flavor --name local
pnv create flavor --name production
```

**Add a secret to an existing YAML.**

```bash
pnv encrypt "the-new-value" --flavor local     # paste the SECRET;... line into envs/app.local.yaml
```

**Full build path.**

```bash
pnv generate env  --directory envs --output dist --flavor production
pnv generate dart --directory dist --output lib/envs --flavor production
flutter build apk $(pnv to-dart-define dist/app.production.env)
```

**Rotate a key.** There is no rotate command. Decrypt every secret with the old key, `delete flavor`,
`create flavor`, re-encrypt each value, replace the tokens. Do the decrypt pass *first* — deleting
the flavor destroys the key.

**Onboard a teammate.** `.pnvrc` and the YAML are already in the repo; they need only the key file
copied into their `storage` directory out of band.

## What must never be committed

- `<storage>/*.key` — the keys. `.gitignore` should carry `*.key`.
- The `.env` output directory — plaintext.
- Safe to commit: `.pnvrc`, the encrypted `*.yaml`, and the generated `*.dart`.

## Source map

| Where to look | For |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/src/pnv_runner.dart` | the command table |
| `lib/src/commands/cryptic_command.dart` | key resolution shared by encrypt/decrypt/generate env |
| `lib/src/commands/encrypt_command.dart`, `lib/src/handlers/decrypt_handler.dart` | the `SECRET;` wire format |
| `lib/src/mixins/file_mixin.dart` | YAML⇒env, env⇒Dart, type inference, `flavorFrom` |
| `lib/src/mixins/pnv_config_mixin.dart` | `.pnvrc` discovery and storage paths |
| `lib/src/models/pnv_config.dart` | config schema, alias resolution, conflict check |
| `lib/src/handlers/flavor_handler.dart` | flavor create/delete |
| `test/e2e/` | executable examples of every command |
